Theme

Latin word

quisque

quisque, quaeque, quodque

pronoun and adjective (as a pronoun, neuter quicque); never first in its clause

each, each one; every (one in a series): every fifth, all the best; each one, everyone (taken one by one)

In this lexicon

  • each

    the recommended word · classical · Cato Agr. 5.5: utī suō quisque locō cubet; Cic. Amic. 62: quot quisque habēret; Traupman 308

  • every

    also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 67: veterrima quaeque; Cic. Verr. 2.2.139: quīntō quōque annō, every fifth year (Lewis & Short); Cic. Rab. Post. 34: tertiō quōque verbō, at every other word (Lewis & Short)

  • everyone

    also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 454: suus cuique mōs; Cic. Amic. 62: caprās et ovēs quot quisque habēret, dīcere posse

  • suus quisque: respectively

    classical

  • prius vīllam videat clausa utī siet, et utī suō quisque locō cubet

    first let him see that the farmhouse is locked, and that each man is sleeping in his own placeCato Agr. 5.5
